statements.t: We have taken, and continue to take, actions intended to mitigate the impact of these disruptions; however, given the dynamic nature of these conditions, we expect continued variability in the macroeconomic environment.

Based upon our history of generating positive cash flows, we believe our existing cash and cash generated from operations will be sufficient to service our current obligations for at least the next 12 months.
However, we cannot assure you that we will be able to obtain additional debt or equity financing on acceptable terms in the future.

On February 17, 2026, our Board approved the 2026 Restructuring Initiative which aims to optimize our operating model, transform our supply chain, reduce complexity, and drive operational efficiencies, while strengthening core capabilities.
We expect to realize annualized pre-tax gross cost savings of approximately $200 million upon completion of the program.
Our estimates of the costs of the initiative and the expected benefits are preliminary estimates and are subject to a number of assumptions, including local law requirements in various jurisdictions.
We expect to continue to pay cash dividends on a quarterly basis.

We expect our future cash requirements will relate to working capital, capital expenditures, restructuring and integration, compensation and benefit-related obligations, interest expense and debt service obligations, litigation costs, the return of capital to shareholders, including through the payment of any dividends, and other contractual obligations that arise in the normal course of business.
As of September 27, 2026, we expect our primary cash requirements for fiscal year 2026 to include capital expenditures.
We will continue to monitor any additional changes to Pillar Two.
We are strongly on track to deliver our business transformation that we began last year.
